messages.subject: Group size "outlier" values
parts:
Hi all,  first of all, thanks for this space where you can find support!

I am analyzing my stratified data, and I am finding troubles regarding uncertainty in my estimates. My estimates' component  percentages of variance are quite high for group size. After a quick check I realized there are some detections of really high group size, around 11% of my dataset presents group values that are considered outliers. I was wondering if it would be ok to delete these detections or if I must go for a covariate analysis to take into account this variation in group size.

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Group size "outlier" values
parts:
Greetings Elena

I don't think it is useful to think of some of your detections as "outliers". They were observations that you made, so it is questionable to remove them from your data.

The CVs associated with your stratum-specific estimates (0.17 and 0.26) are not extreme. Looking at the variance components table, note that variability in group size accounts for 20% and 36% of the uncertainty in abundance estimates in the respective strata. Meaning, that even if you did "shrink" variability in group size somehow, the main source of uncertainty (encounter rate variability between transects) would still remain.

Fitting models with group size as a covariate in the detection function is not likely to have an effect upon uncertainty in your estimates. The covariate modelling will change the point estimates of individual abundance, because size bias in the estimate of average group size in the population may exist. Recall size bias is caused by small groups at large distances being missed, resulting in the average group size in your observed sample being too large.

In summary, I would not suggest removing detections as outliers and applying group size as a covariate will address the size bias issue, but not the variability in observed group sizes.
